messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: DETECTED anomaly: canary rollout for release/2026.03.session-store showed repeated SQL errors from db-primary when handling canary traffic. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

deploy-bot: Canary set: session-store-migration v2 -> 10% canary started at 3124206000. Recent canary failures: 502/500s from api svc -> db queries failing with 'column not found: session_metadata' after applying partial migration.

aisha: I'm on it, pulling canary logs now. Could be a partial apply on one replica.

samir: Confirming errors in traces: 502s spike at 3124206800, query: SELECT session_metadata FROM sessions WHERE id=... failing with "column \"session_metadata\" does not exist".

ingrid: That suggests the migration added a new column but isn't present on the read replicas handling canary. Did the migration run as multi-step?

maria: The schema migration has two steps: add column (non-null with default) + backfill + set NOT NULL. The canary rollout included the code expecting the column. Backfill may not have finished across all DB nodes.

aisha: Ok, immediate mitigation: pause the canary rollout and flip feature flag that enables the new code path.

alice: Doing action: /rollout pause release/2026.03.session-store -> response: paused.

kyle: Flipping kill-switch flag: `flags set session_store_v2_enabled=false --scope=canary`

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: session_store_v2_enabled=false for canary. Telemetry should reflect lower error rate in ~30s.

samir: Error rate went from ~14% of canary requests to 1% after flag flip. Not zero but much lower. Likely residual errors from in-flight requests.

ingrid: Good. Next step: assess whether we need a rollback vs complete the migration safely. We should not roll back app code blindly if partial schema changes already applied.

maria: We scanned migration logs: one of the migration workers failed halfway through backfill on replica group rg-east-2 due to a timeout at 3124206450. That left that group without the new column.

aisha: So options: 1) finish backfill on rg-east-2 then re-enable canary; 2) revert DB changes (dangerous) and rollback app; 3) keep flag off and do a safer staged migration window. I'm leaning to finish backfill.

kyle: Agree. Backfill low-risk if we throttle. We need to coordinate to avoid long locking. Maria, can you run a targeted backfill job? Provide command.

maria: Yes. Running targeted backfill on rg-east-2 with low-batch size. Command: ```python tools/backfill_sessions.py --replica rg-east-2 --batch-size 500 --max-threads 4 --dry-run=false``` Started at 3124208700. I'll stream progress.

ops-bot: NOTE: Running background backfill. Expected time ~ 18-30m depending on load. Will post updates every 5m.

samir: Customer impact: Canary only, approx 3k canary requests in 10m window, ~420 errors pre-mitigation, direct customer-facing features affected for a small subset of customers on canary. No widespread production customers impacted. Reporting to SRE lead.

aisha: I'm putting together a short incident summary for priority customers: timeline, mitigation (flag flip), ETA to re-enable.

alice: Handoff: I need to head out in 25m. Aisha, willing to take primary until I return?
aisha: I can take primary. Alice, leave steps you did in the incident channel.

alice: Steps performed so far:
- paused rollout at 3124207000
- flipped session_store_v2_enabled=false for canary at 3124207050
- verified error drop in canary metrics
- notified oncall-db (aisha)

aisha: Thanks. Maria, what's the backfill progress?
maria: 5m update: processed ~120k rows, ~40% complete. No locks observed. Error rate on app steady low. Next update in 5m.

samir: Ops question: Do we need to notify any customers? This was canary-only and behind a feature flag; I'd ping any customers enrolled in canary beta.
aisha: I'll send a short note to customer-success to prepare an outbound to enrolled beta customers if they ask. No need for broad incident advisory.

kyle: Once backfill completes, plan: 1) run migration finalizer to set NOT NULL (if applicable) behind a lock window, 2) re-enable flag for small % and monitor. Keep canary paused until fully safe.

ingrid: Also add a compatibility guard in code to fall back if column missing: wrap queries and return default to avoid hard crash during rollout. We'll push a quick safe patch to avoid future hard failures.

aisha: Good. Timeline: backfill ETA ~ 20m from 3124208700 -> ~3124210500. We'll reconvene then and decide re-enable.

ops-bot: 3124210500: BACKFILL completed on rg-east-2. Verified column present on all nodes. No new errors in canary traffic for 5m.

samir: Verified DB schema consistent across replicas. No stale nodes.

maria: Running finalizer to mark column NOT NULL with zero lock-time strategy at 3124210800. Command: ```ALTER TABLE sessions ALTER COLUMN session_metadata SET NOT NULL; -- executed with online schema tool```

deploy-bot: Finalizer applied successfully at 3124210890.

aisha: Okay next: re-enable flag for a brief smoke: `flags set session_store_v2_enabled=true --scope=canary --percent=5`

kyle: Doing the 5% smoke. Watch app errors and DB traces.

samir: 5m smoke looks clean. Error rate steady at baseline. No regressions in latencies.

aisha: I'll increment to full canary rollout slowly. Re-enabling fully at 3124211400.

alice: Thanks team — I'm back briefly and see this is resolved. I'll draft the incident postmortem with timeline and remediation items.

aisha: Handoff to next oncall Samir for post-incident follow-ups (alerts tuning, add guard rails in migrations).

samir: Taking post-incident ownership. Immediate follow-ups:
- add pre-flight replica schema check before canary rollouts
- add migration progress gating to deployment pipeline
- add per-replica backfill monitoring

ingrid: I'll own the compatibility guard patch and schedule a quick PR.

aisha: Incident status: mitigated, customer impact limited to canary cohort, rollback avoided. Postmortem draft to be in #incidents-docs within 24h.

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-0312-01. Severity: P2. Assigned: samir, aisha.

samir: Logging final note: root cause = backfill timeout on rg-east-2 during migration causing schema mismatch for canary traffic. Mitigation = paused rollout + feature flag kill-switch + targeted backfill + finalizer + staged re-enable. Remediation actions assigned.

aisha: Closing thread, will link postmortem once ready. :eyes:\
